q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT DISTINCT(EMAIL) FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT(EMAIL) FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
counterexample: INSERT INTO PERSON (ID, EMAIL) VALUES (1, 'example@example.com'); INSERT INTO PERSON (ID, EMAIL) VALUES (2, 'Example@example.com');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 uses GROUP BY and HAVING to find emails that appear more than once, while Q2 uses DISTINCT and GROUP BY to achieve the same result. The key difference is that Q1 does not use DISTINCT, which can lead to incorrect results if the same email appears in different cases or with leading/trailing spaces.
